---1f:T2eff,### 1.1 What a Bank Does: The Balance-Sheet Model [FOUNDATION]

A bank is a specialized financial intermediary. It accepts deposits from savers, raises wholesale borrowings, maintains liquid statutory reserves, invests in marketable securities, and originates credit advances. Its economic role is to perform **maturity transformation** (borrowing short-term to lend long-term), **liquidity transformation** (converting liquid deposits into illiquid loans), and **risk transformation** (absorbing diversified credit risk).

#### Master Bank Balance Sheet Architecture
| Assets (Uses of Funds — What the World Owes the Bank) | Liabilities & Equity (Sources of Funds — What the Bank Owes) |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Cash & Balances with RBI**: CRR cash deposits, vault cash, interbank balances | **Customer Deposits**: Demand deposits (Current, Savings) & Time deposits (FD, RD) |
| **Investments**: Approved G-Secs (SLR), T-Bills, corporate bonds, equity shares | **Borrowings**: Liquidity adjustment borrowings from RBI (Repo/MSF), interbank loans |
| **Loans & Advances**: Retail credit, MSME loans, corporate credit, agri advances | **Other Liabilities & Provisions**: Accrued interest, tax provisions, unpaid expenses |
| **Fixed & Other Assets**: Bank premises, digital IT infrastructure, deferred tax assets | **Capital & Reserves (Net Worth)**: Common equity (CET1), reserves, retained earnings |

$$\mathbf{Total\ Assets = Total\ Liabilities + Regulatory\ Equity\ (Net\ Worth)}$$

> 💡 **Core Insight:** A customer deposit is a **liability of the bank** because the bank is contractually obligated to repay the depositor. A loan is an **asset of the bank** because the borrower is contractually indebted to the bank. Interest paid on deposits is an operational funding cost; interest and processing fees earned on loans represent primary operating revenue.

---

### 1.2 Liquidity, Solvency, and Profitability: The Three Cardinal Pillars [FOUNDATION]

* **Liquidity**: The capacity to meet cash-flow and withdrawal obligations promptly as they fall due. A bank can be fully solvent (assets far exceeding liabilities) but become instantly **illiquid** if depositors trigger a sudden run and its assets cannot be converted into cash without catastrophic fire-sale losses.
* **Solvency**: The structural condition where the fair economic value of a bank's assets exceeds its total liabilities to external creditors, underpinned by sufficient loss-absorbing capital. Persistent loan defaults and credit impairments destroy equity capital, eventually rendering the bank **insolvent**.
* **Profitability**: The ability to generate net positive earnings after funding costs, operational expenses, loan-loss provisions, and taxes. A bank can be liquid and solvent today, yet suffer chronic unprofitability that progressively erodes capital over time.

---

### 1.3 Deposit Categories & CASA Dynamics [FOUNDATION]

| Deposit Category | Statutory Nature | Interest Earning Mechanics | Primary Use & Exam Distinction |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Current Account** | Pure Demand Liability | Zero interest under standard domestic banking rules | Designed for commercial entities, traders, and businesses requiring frequent daily transaction turnover |
| **Savings Account** | Demand Liability | Compounded interest calculated on **daily end-of-day balances** | Designed for individuals, households, and eligible charitable trusts; combines savings yield with payment access |
| **Fixed / Term Deposit** | Time Liability | Fixed contractual interest; premature withdrawal subject to penal interest | Funds placed for a fixed tenor (7 days to 10 years); higher interest yielding longer-term funding stability |
| **Recurring Deposit** | Time Liability | Regular monthly fixed installments over a defined horizon | Disciplined savings vehicle building a lumpsum maturity corpus |
| **CASA Ratio** | Funding Metric | $$\mathbf{CASA\ Ratio = \frac{Current\ Deposits + Savings\ Deposits}{Total\ Deposits} \times 100}$$ | A high CASA ratio provides low-cost operational funding, lowering the bank's blended Cost of Funds (CoF) |

---

### 1.4 How a Bank Earns Money: NII & Net Interest Margin (NIM) [FOUNDATION]

A commercial bank's income statement is governed by two core components:
1. **Net Interest Income (NII)**:
   $$\mathbf{NII = Interest\ Income\ (from\ loans\ \&\ investments) - Interest\ Expense\ (paid\ on\ deposits\ \&\ borrowings)}$$
2. **Net Interest Margin (NIM)**:
   $$\mathbf{NIM = \frac{Net\ Interest\ Income\ (NII)}{Average\ Earning\ Assets} \times 100}$$
3. **Operating Profit & Net Profit**:
   $$\mathbf{Operating\ Profit = NII + Non\text{-}Interest\ Income\ (fees,\ commissions,\ treasury\ gains) - Operating\ Expenses\ (opex)}$$
   $$\mathbf{Net\ Profit\ (PAT) = Operating\ Profit - Loan\ Loss\ Provisions\ (credit\ costs) - Corporate\ Taxes}$$

---

### 1.5 Credit Creation Mechanics: Safe Conceptual Model [FOUNDATION]

When a commercial bank sanctions a credit facility and disburses loan proceeds, it does not physically hand over bags of currency; instead, it opens a credit ledger entry and **credits the borrower's deposit account**. In doing so, the commercial banking system **creates fresh deposits**. 

Credit creation is not infinite or mechanical:
- The textbook **Money Multiplier ($1 / \text{CRR}$)** is an illustrative theoretical abstraction.
- In reality, commercial bank lending is strictly bounded by **capital adequacy requirements (CRAR)**, **regulatory liquidity mandates (LCR, NSFR, SLR)**, **creditworthy borrower demand**, **internal risk appetite**, and **profitability constraints**. Banks do not lend simply because they hold excess reserve balances.

---

### 1.6 Master Banking Ratios Matrix [FOUNDATION]

| Regulatory / Financial Ratio | Mathematical Formula & Meaning | What It Does NOT Tell You on Its Own |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Net Interest Margin (NIM)** | $\frac{\text{NII}}{\text{Average Earning Assets}} \times 100$ (spread efficiency) | Does not reflect underlying credit risk, borrower default rates, or provision costs |
| **CASA Ratio** | $\frac{\text{CASA Deposits}}{\text{Total Deposits}} \times 100$ (low-cost deposit share) | Does not measure overall balance sheet asset quality, solvency, or net bottom-line profit |
| **Gross NPA Ratio** | $\frac{\text{Gross NPAs}}{\text{Gross Advances}} \times 100$ (total delinquent loans) | Does not account for loan-loss provisions already built up to absorb potential write-offs |
| **Net NPA Ratio** | $\frac{\text{Gross NPAs} - \text{Cumulative Provisions}}{\text{Net Advances}} \times 100$ (uncovered bad debt) | Cannot be compared across banks without verifying individual provisioning coverage policies |
| **CRAR / Capital Adequacy** | $\frac{\text{Eligible Capital (Tier 1 + Tier 2)}}{\text{Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA)}} \times 100$ | Is NOT capital divided by total unweighted assets; weights vary heavily by asset risk |
| **Return on Assets (ROA)** | $\frac{\text{Net Profit after Tax}}{\text{Average Total Assets}} \times 100$ (asset efficiency) | Can be inflated by high-risk volatile treasury trading gains or one-off asset sales |
| **Return on Equity (ROE)** | $\frac{\text{Net Profit after Tax}}{\text{Average Shareholder Equity}} \times 100$ (equity return) | High ROE can merely reflect dangerous financial leverage (holding very thin equity capital) |
| **Cost-to-Income Ratio** | $\frac{\text{Operating Expenses (excluding provisions)}}{\text{Total Operating Income (NII + Other Income)}} \times 100$ | Lower is not always better if the bank is dangerously under-investing in cybersecurity or risk controls |

---

### 1.7 Master Financial Message Codes & Standard Formats [FOUNDATION + RULE-SENSITIVE]

| Code / Identifier | Length & Type | Canonical Structure & Decomposition | Regulatory Mandate & Application Threshold |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **MICR** *(Magnetic Ink Character Recognition)* | **9** Numeric Digits | `3 (City Code / 1st 3 PIN digits)` + `3 (Bank Code)` + `3 (Branch Code)` | Printed at cheque bottom in magnetic ink (E-13B font) for automated clearing (CTS) under NI Act, 1881 |
| **PAN** *(Permanent Account Number)* | **10** Alphanumeric | 5 Letters + 4 Digits + 1 Letter.<br>• **4th char** = Entity Status: `P` (Individual/Person), `C` (Company), `F` (Firm), `H` (HUF), `A` (AOP), `T` (Trust), `B` (BOI), `J` (Artificial Juridical Person)<br>• **5th char** = 1st letter of Holder's Surname / Entity Name | Statutory direct tax identification under Section 139A of Income-tax Act, 1961 / Income-tax Act, 2025 (CBDT) |
| **IFSC** *(Indian Financial System Code)* | **11** Alphanumeric | `4 (Bank Identity)` + **`0` (Fixed Zero, reserved for future use)** + `6 (Branch Identity)` | Mandatory routing code for electronic interbank clearing in NEFT, RTGS, and IMPS (RBI) |
| **PRAN** *(Permanent Retirement Account Number)* | **12** Numeric Digits | Unique lifetime portable retirement account identifier | National Pension System (NPS) & Atal Pension Yojana (APY) under PFRDA |
| **UAN** *(Universal Account Number)* | **12** Numeric Digits | Unique lifetime portable identifier for formal sector workforce | Mandatory account registry under Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) |
| **GSTIN** *(GST Identification Number)* | **15** Alphanumeric | `2 (State Code: e.g. 07 Delhi, 27 MH)` + `10 (PAN of Entity)` + `1 (Entity No)` + `1 ('Z' by default)` + `1 (Check digit)` | Statutory indirect tax registration under CGST / SGST / IGST Acts (CBIC) |
| **NEFT UTR** *(Unique Transaction Reference)* | **16** Alphanumeric | Unique sequential identifier generated per interbank batch clearing transaction | National Electronic Funds Transfer (RBI half-hourly batch clearing system) |
| **LEI** *(Legal Entity Identifier)* | **20** Alphanumeric | Global ISO 17442 standard identifier for entities participating in financial transactions | **Dual Mandatory Regulatory Thresholds:**<br>1. **Credit Exposure $\ge$ ₹5 Crore**: Non-individual borrowers across SCBs, AIFIs, NBFCs (barred from credit renewal/enhancement if missing)<br>2. **Single Remittance $\ge$ ₹50 Crore**: Cross-border capital/current transactions under FEMA |
| **RTGS UTR** *(Unique Transaction Reference)* | **22** Alphanumeric | `4 (Bank IFSC)` + `1 ('R' for RTGS)` + `1 (Channel: 'C' Customer, 'I' Inter-bank, 'P' Participant)` + `8 (Date: YYYYMMDD)` + `8 (Sequential Running No: nnnnnnnn)` | Real-Time Gross Settlement system governed by RBI RTGS System Regulations |
| **EPF Establishment ID** | **22** Alphanumeric | Region Code (3) + Office Code (3) + Establishment Code (7) + Extension Code (3) | EPFO employer establishment identification & compliance registry |
| **SWIFT / BIC** *(Business Identifier Code)* | **8 or 11** Alphanumeric | `4 (Bank Code)` + `2 (Country Code: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2)` + `2 (Location Code)` + `[3 Optional Branch Code]` | Global financial messaging under ISO 9362; International Headquarters: **La Hulpe, Belgium** |
| **Card-on-File Tokenisation (CoFT)** | Token Identifier | Substitutes a unique algorithmic token for actual 16-digit card PAN | Merchants and payment aggregators strictly barred from storing actual card numbers; managed via bank portal |

> ⚠️ **EXAM ANGLE:**
> - **The RTGS vs NEFT Length Trap**: RTGS UTR is **22 characters**; NEFT UTR is **16 characters** (examiners routinely swap these two numbers).
> - **RTGS Anatomy Trap**: Format is: **4 IFSC + 1 System (R) + 1 Channel (C) + 8 Date (YYYYMMDD) + 8 Sequence = 22** (Notice: 8-digit running sequence, not 9; 5th is 'R', 6th is Channel).
> - **LEI Dual-Threshold Trap**: Borrower credit exposure threshold is **$\ge$ ₹5 Crore**; cross-border FEMA remittance threshold is **$\ge$ ₹50 Crore per transaction**.
> - **IFSC 5th Character**: The 5th character is always numeric **0 (zero)**, NEVER the alphabetical letter 'O'.
> - **MICR Sequence**: MICR 9-digit sequence is **City Code (3) $\to$ Bank Code (3) $\to$ Branch Code (3)** (City matches first 3 digits of PIN).

---20:T1817,### 2.1 From Presidency Banks to State Bank of India [FOUNDATION]

| Historical Epoch / Entity | Key Date / Year | Structural Transformation & Constituent Banks | Statutory Authority & Equity Holdings |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Presidency Banks** | 1806, 1840, 1843 | • **Bank of Calcutta** (founded 1806, renamed **Bank of Bengal** 1809)<br>• **Bank of Bombay** (founded 1840)<br>• **Bank of Madras** (founded 1843) | British Crown chartered provincial banking entities with autonomous note-issuing privileges |
| **Imperial Bank of India** | **27 January 1921** | Tripartite amalgamation of Bank of Bengal, Bank of Bombay, and Bank of Madras into a single commercial banking entity | Enacted under Imperial Bank of India Act, 1920 (acted as banker to government before RBI) |
| **State Bank of India (SBI)** | **1 July 1955** | Conversion of Imperial Bank of India into the **State Bank of India** | Enacted under **State Bank of India Act, 1955** on the statutory recommendations of the **All India Rural Credit Survey Committee (chaired by A.D. Gorwala)**.<br>*(RBI originally subscribed 60% equity; Government of India acquired RBI stake in 2007)* |

### 2.2 The Two Epochs of Bank Nationalisation [FOUNDATION]

| Nationalisation Wave | Effective Date | Deposit Threshold Mandate | Scope & Number of Banks | Governing Statute & Historical Context |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **First Wave** | **19 July 1969** | Aggregate public deposits $\ge$ **₹50 Crore** | **14 Major Commercial Banks** | Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 *(Indira Gandhi premiership)* |
| **Second Wave** | **15 April 1980** | Aggregate public deposits $\ge$ **₹200 Crore** | **6 Commercial Banks** | Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980 |

> 💡 **Legal Nuance:** The nationalisation takeovers occurred on **19 July 1969** and **15 April 1980**, while the corresponding parliamentary Acts bear the titles 1970 and 1980. Do not confuse the effective executive takeover date with the year of statutory enactment.

### 2.3 Master Statutory Banking Architecture & Core Anchor Sections [RULE-SENSITIVE]

| Governing Statute | Key Section | Legal Mandate & Core Operational Provision | High-Yield Parameters & Examiner Traps |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934** | **Section 17** | **Legitimate Business of RBI** | Defines authorized central banking, rediscounting, and sovereign financial operations |
| | **Section 22** | **Exclusive Banknote Issuance** | Confers exclusive authority to issue currency banknotes in India *(except ₹1 notes and coins issued by MoF)* |
| | **Section 24** | **Maximum Denomination Ceiling** | Authorizes RBI to issue banknotes up to **₹10,000** *(Coinage Act, 2011 authorizes coins up to **₹1,000**)* |
| | **Section 42(1)** | **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** | Mandates SCBs to maintain CRR cash balances with RBI as % of NDTL *(RBI pays **0% interest** on CRR)* |
| | **Sections 45-ZB to 45-ZG** | **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** | Codifies composition (6 members: 3 RBI, 3 Central Govt), 4-year non-renewable tenure, 4-member quorum |
| **Banking Regulation Act, 1949** | **Section 5(b)** | **Statutory Definition of 'Banking'** | Accepting, for lending or investment, of deposits of money from public, repayable on demand/otherwise |
| | **Section 22** | **Mandatory Bank Licensing** | Mandatory license from RBI required to commence or carry on banking business in India |
| | **Section 24** | **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** | Mandates banks to maintain unencumbered liquid assets (gold, G-Secs, cash) against NDTL *(Statutory ceiling: **40%**; operational: 18%)* |
| | **Section 35A** | **Comprehensive Direction Powers** | Comprehensive power empowering RBI to issue binding executive directions to all banks in public interest |
| | **Section 49A** | **Cheque Acceptance Restriction** | Restricts acceptance of deposits withdrawable by cheque strictly to licensed banking institutions |
| **Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881** | **Section 4** | **Promissory Note** | Unconditional undertaking in writing signed by maker to pay a certain sum of money |
| | **Section 5** | **Bill of Exchange** | Unconditional order in writing signed by maker directing a certain person to pay a certain sum |
| | **Section 6** | **Cheque & Truncation** | Bill of exchange drawn on a specified banker, payable on demand *(includes electronic image under CTS)* |
| | **Section 138** | **Criminal Dishonour of Cheque** | Penal sanction for dishonour due to insufficiency of funds: **Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine up to twice cheque amount, or both** |
| **Other Core Financial Statutes** | **FEMA, 1999** | **Foreign Exchange Regulation** | Governs cross-border current and capital account transactions |
| | **PMLA, 2002** | **Anti-Money Laundering & KYC** | Mandates KYC, client verification, and suspicious transaction reporting (STR) to FIU-IND |
| | **IBC, 2016** | **Insolvency & Resolution** | Time-bound corporate insolvency resolution and liquidation framework via NCLT |
| | **SARFAESI Act, 2002** | **Secured Asset Enforcement** | Enables secured creditors to enforce security interests out-of-court without civil suit |
| | **Income-tax Act, 2025** | **Direct Tax Overhaul (eff. 1 April 2026)** | Slashes sections from 819 to 536; modernizes direct tax administration, forms, and TDS mappings |
| | **Sabka Bima Act, 2025** | **Insurance Laws Overhaul (commenced 5 Feb 2026)** | Amends Insurance Act 1938 & IRDA Act 1999; permits **100% FDI** under automatic route |

> ⚠️ **EXAM ANGLE:**
> - **The CRR vs SLR Act Trap**: CRR is governed by **Section 42 of RBI Act 1934**; SLR is governed by **Section 24 of Banking Regulation Act 1949**.
> - **Note vs Coin Statutory Ceilings**: Maximum banknote denomination is **₹10,000** (RBI Act Sec 24); maximum coin denomination is **₹1,000** (Coinage Act 2011 Sec 6).
> - **SBI Genesis Committee**: Converted from Imperial Bank on **1 July 1955** under SBI Act 1955 following the **All India Rural Credit Survey Committee (A.D. Gorwala Committee)**.

---22:T2377,### 4.1 RBI Central Board of Directors [FOUNDATION]

The governance and general superintendence of the Reserve Bank of India are vested in the Central Board of Directors under **Section 8 of the RBI Act, 1934**.
- **Statutory Composition (Maximum 21 Members)**:
  - **Governor** and up to **4 Deputy Governors** (appointed under Section 8(1)(a)).
  - **4 Directors** nominated from the 4 Local Boards (Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, New Delhi).
  - **2 Government Officials** (typically Economic Affairs Secretary and Financial Services Secretary from MoF).
  - **10 Non-Official Directors** nominated by the Government of India representing diverse economic fields.
- **Tenure**: Official directors (Governor/DGs) hold office for terms up to 5 years and are eligible for reappointment.

---

### 4.2 Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) Framework [FOUNDATION + RULE-SENSITIVE]

The MPC is a statutory committee constituted under **Sections 45-ZB to 45-ZG of the RBI Act, 1934** (amended via Finance Act, 2016).

| Parameter | Statutory Rule & Legal Mandate |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Total Membership** | **6 Members** |
| **RBI Members (3)** | • **Governor** (ex-officio Chairperson)<br>• **Deputy Governor** in charge of Monetary Policy<br>• **One Officer** of the RBI nominated by the Central Board |
| **External Members (3)** | Appointed by the Central Government on the recommendations of a Cabinet Search-cum-Selection Committee |
| **External Member Tenure** | Fixed **4-year term**; **STRICTLY NOT eligible for reappointment** |
| **Meeting Quorum** | Minimum **4 members**, with at least the Governor or Deputy Governor in attendance |
| **Voting Mechanics** | Each member has one vote; the **Governor holds a second / casting vote** in the event of an equality of votes (tie) |
| **Publication of Minutes** | Minutes, member rationale, and individual voting records must be published on the **14th day** after the meeting under Section 45ZL |

---

### 4.3 Monetary Policy Objective: Flexible Inflation Targeting [FOUNDATION]

Under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act, the primary objective of monetary policy is to **maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth**.
- **Nominal Anchor**: **Consumer Price Index (CPI - Combined)**, NEVER WPI.
- **Inflation Target**: **4.00%** with a statutory tolerance band of **±2.00%** (lower tolerance limit: **2.00%**; upper tolerance limit: **6.00%**).
- **Failure to Meet Target**: Defined as average headline CPI inflation remaining outside the 2%–6% band for **three consecutive quarters**. If failed, RBI must submit a statutory report to the Central Government explaining causes, remedial actions, and an estimated time-frame for convergence.

---

### 4.4 Policy Rate & Liquidity Corridor Tools [RULE-SENSITIVE]

```
Corridor Ceiling:  Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) Rate / Bank Rate  [Repo + 25 bps]
                                     ▲
Policy Anchor:                 Repo Rate                              [Operating Benchmark]
                                     ▼
Corridor Floor:    Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) Rate               [Repo - 25 bps]
```

| Operational Tool | Economic Mechanism | Transmission Mechanics & Governing Rules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Policy Repo Rate** | Key policy benchmark signal | Rate at which RBI lends short-term liquidity to banks against eligible government collateral (G-Secs) |
| **Standing Deposit Facility (SDF)** | Liquidity absorption floor | Uncollateralized facility allowing banks to park overnight liquidity with RBI; absorbs surplus cash without pledging G-Secs |
| **Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)** | Liquidity injection ceiling | Emergency penal overnight borrowing window for banks against approved G-Secs dipping into their SLR buffer up to permitted limit |
| **Bank Rate** | Statutory benchmark | Long-term reference rate under Section 49 of RBI Act; penal rate linked to discounting of bills and banking penalties |
| **Open Market Operations (OMO)** | Outright liquidity tool | Outright purchase (injects durable cash) or sale (absorbs durable cash) of government securities by RBI |
| **VRR / VRRR Auctions** | Fine-tuning operations | Variable Rate Repo (injects liquidity) and Variable Rate Reverse Repo (absorbs liquidity) for non-standard tenors |

#### Master Comparison: Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) vs Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)
| Dimension | Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) | Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Governing Statute** | **Section 42(1), RBI Act 1934** | **Section 24, Banking Regulation Act 1949** |
| **Maintenance Medium** | Strictly **Cash Balances** | **Approved Liquid Assets**: Cash, Gold, unencumbered approved G-Secs / T-Bills |
| **Custody Location** | Deposited and maintained **with RBI** | Maintained by the bank **on its own balance sheet** |
| **Interest Return** | **0% Interest** (RBI pays zero interest on CRR) | Bank earns interest/coupons and yield on underlying G-Secs and gold holdings |
| **Statutory Floor & Ceiling** | 2006 Amendment removed earlier 3% floor and 20% ceiling; RBI has complete discretion | Statutory ceiling capped at **40%** (2007 amendment removed earlier 25% floor) |
| **Operational Benchmark** | Policy variable | Capped at statutory ceiling; operational rate maintained at **18.00%** |

---

### 4.5 Sovereign Cash Management & Public Debt Instruments [RULE-SENSITIVE]

* **Ways and Means Advances (WMA)**:
  - Clean, short-term advances extended by RBI to Central and State Governments under **Section 17(5) of RBI Act, 1934** to bridge temporary cash-flow mismatches between expenditure and receipts.
  - Repayable within a maximum of **3 months (90 days)**.
  - Overdraft (OD) facility is permitted beyond WMA limits for specified operational days.
* **Treasury Bills (T-Bills)**:
  - Short-term sovereign debt instruments issued by the Government of India, issued at a discount and redeemed at par (face value).
  - Issued in three standard tenors: **91-day**, **182-day**, and **364-day**.
  - Minimum investment: **₹10,000** and in multiples thereof; auctioned weekly on Wednesdays.
* **Cash Management Bills (CMBs)**:
  - Ultra short-term discounted sovereign instruments issued to meet temporary cash mismatches; maturities are strictly **less than 91 days**.
* **Dated Government Securities (G-Secs) & Bond Yield Mechanics**:
  - Long-term fixed or floating-rate sovereign bonds with maturities from 2 years up to 40+ years.
  - **Inverse Price-Yield Relationship**: When market interest rates/yields rise, the market price of existing fixed-coupon bonds **falls**; when yields decline, bond prices **rise**. Longer duration bonds experience greater price volatility for a given yield shift.

---

### 4.6 Monetary & Liquidity Aggregates: Classical vs Modern [FOUNDATION]

#### 1. Classical Monetary Aggregates (M0 to M4)
* **Reserve Money ($M_0$)** *(Monetary Base / High-Powered Money)*:
  $$\mathbf{M_0 = Currency\ in\ Circulation\ (CIC) + Bankers'\ Deposits\ with\ RBI + 'Other'\ Deposits\ with\ RBI}$$
* **Narrow Money ($M_1$)** *(Most Liquid Commercial Money)*:
  $$\mathbf{M_1 = Currency\ with\ the\ Public + Demand\ Deposits\ with\ Banking\ System\ (CASA) + 'Other'\ Deposits\ with\ RBI}$$
  *(Note: Currency with the Public = Currency in Circulation minus Cash in hand with banks)*
* **Intermediate Money ($M_2$)**:
  $$\mathbf{M_2 = M_1 + Savings\ Deposits\ with\ Post\ Office\ Savings\ Banks}$$
* **Broad Money ($M_3$)** *(Standard Policy Aggregate tracked by RBI)*:
  $$\mathbf{M_3 = M_1 + Time\ Deposits\ with\ the\ Banking\ System\ (Fixed\ \&\ Recurring\ Deposits)}$$
* **Comprehensive Money ($M_4$)**:
  $$\mathbf{M_4 = M_3 + Total\ Post\ Office\ Deposits\ (EXCLUDING\ National\ Savings\ Certificates\ /\ NSC)}$$

#### 2. Modern New Monetary & Liquidity Aggregates (Dr. Y.V. Reddy Committee, 1998)
* **$NM_1$**: Currency with the Public + Demand Deposits with Banking System + 'Other' Deposits with RBI.
* **$NM_2$**: $NM_1$ + Short-Term Time Deposits of residents (contractual maturity up to 1 year).
* **$NM_3$**: $NM_2$ + Long-Term Time Deposits of residents (maturity $> 1$ year) + Call/Term Borrowings from Financial Institutions.
* **$L_1$**: $NM_3$ + All Deposits with Post Office Savings Banks (**EXCLUDING NSC**).
* **$L_2$**: $L_1$ + Term Deposits with Term Lending / Refinance Institutions (NABARD, EXIM Bank, SIDBI, NHB) + Term Borrowings by FIs + CDs issued by FIs.
* **$L_3$**: $L_2$ + Public Deposits accepted by Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs).
* **Money Multiplier ($m$)**:
  $$\mathbf{m = \frac{Broad\ Money\ (M_3)}{Reserve\ Money\ (M_0)}}$$

> ⚠️ **EXAM ANGLE:**
> - **M0 vs M1 Currency Component**: $M_0$ contains **Currency in Circulation**; $M_1$ contains **Currency with the Public** (excludes commercial bank vault cash).
> - **The Post Office NSC Trap**: National Savings Certificates (NSC) are **strictly excluded** from both $M_4$ and $L_1$ calculations.
> - **MPC Minutes Timeline**: Statutory deadline for minutes publication is the **14th day** following the MPC meeting.

---23:T1ccb,### 5.1 Interbank Payment Rails & Settlement Architectures [FOUNDATION + RULE-SENSITIVE]

| Payment System | Operator / Oversight | Core Settlement Architecture | Transaction Slabs & Hours | High-Yield Exam Distinction |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **NEFT** | Reserve Bank of India (RBI) | **Deferred Net Settlement (DNS)** in half-hourly batches | **24×7×365**; zero statutory minimum or maximum limit | Account-to-account transfer batched every 30 minutes; NOT real-time |
| **RTGS** | Reserve Bank of India (RBI) | **Real-Time Gross Settlement** (individual gross settlement without netting) | **24×7×365**; **Minimum ₹2 Lakh**; zero RBI-imposed maximum ceiling | High-value instantaneous settlement directly across central bank reserve accounts |
| **IMPS** | NPCI | Instant real-time interbank electronic fund transfer | **24×7×365**; standard ceiling ₹5 Lakh per transaction | Retail instant payment rail accessible via mobile, net-banking, and ATMs |
| **UPI** | NPCI | Interoperable mobile payment overlay using Virtual Payment Address (VPA) / mobile proxy | Instant retail rail; standard limit ₹1 Lakh (₹5 Lakh for hospitals, educational institutions, capital markets, tax) | Payment protocol/rail linking bank accounts; NOT a bank account itself |
| **NACH** | NPCI | Bulk, recurring interbank electronic transaction clearing | Operates clearing batches for dividend, salary, subsidy, and auto-debit mandates | Replaced legacy Electronic Clearing Service (ECS) |
| **AePS** | NPCI | Aadhaar-authenticated banking transactions via Micro-ATMs / BCs | Financial (cash withdrawal, deposit, transfer) and non-financial (balance inquiry) | Uses biometric fingerprints/iris authentication for financial inclusion |
| **CTS** | RBI | Cheque Truncation System (electronic image exchange) | Cleared across 3 regional grids (Northern, Western, Southern Grids) | Replaces physical movement of paper cheques; legally recognized under NI Act Sec 6 |
| **TReDS** | RBI Authorized Entities | Electronic factoring and discounting platform for MSME trade receivables | Connects MSME sellers, corporate/govt buyers, and institutional financiers | Facilitates competitive bidding on trade bills; not a deposit-taking entity |

---

### 5.2 ATM Free Limits, Interchange Fees & Failed Transaction Turnaround (SLA) [RULE-SENSITIVE]

* **Free Monthly ATM Transaction Quota**:
  - **Own-Bank ATMs**: Minimum **5 free transactions per month** (financial + non-financial).
  - **Other-Bank ATMs (6 Designated Metros)**: Minimum **3 free transactions per month** (*Metros: Mumbai, New Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad*).
  - **Other-Bank ATMs (Non-Metro Centers)**: Minimum **5 free transactions per month**.
* **Interchange Fee Caps (between banks)**: Financial transaction cap: **₹17**; Non-financial transaction cap: **₹6**.
* **Customer Charge Ceiling**: Maximum customer fee after exhausting free limits: **₹21** plus applicable taxes.
* **Failed Transaction Reversal SLA & Statutory Compensation**:
  - When an account is debited but cash is not dispensed at an ATM, the bank must auto-reverse the transaction within **T+5 calendar days** ($T = \text{Transaction Date}$).
  - For any delay beyond $T+5$ calendar days, the bank is statutorily mandated to pay compensation of **₹100 per day of delay** directly to the customer's account without requiring a customer grievance.

---

### 5.3 Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026 (RB-IOS 2026) [RULE-SENSITIVE]

The **Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (RB-IOS), 2026** replaced the 2021 framework with effect from **1 July 2026**, strengthening the cost-free, non-adversarial grievance-redress framework.

| Parameter | Predecessor Regime (RB-IOS 2021) | Operative Regime (RB-IOS 2026 — Eff. 1 July 2026) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Centralized Intake Portal** | CRPC, RBI Chandigarh (CMS portal) | **CRPC, RBI Chandigarh** ([cms.rbi.org.in](https://cms.rbi.org.in/)) |
| **Direct Consequential Financial Loss Compensation** | Up to **₹20 Lakh** maximum | Enhanced to **₹30 Lakh** maximum |
| **Compensation for Mental Harassment / Loss of Time** | Up to **₹1 Lakh** additional | Enhanced to **₹3 Lakh** additional |
| **Maximum Total Composite Award** | **₹21 Lakh** (₹20L + ₹1L) | **₹33 Lakh** (₹30L + ₹3L) |
| **Filing Limitation Window** | Within 1 year after bank rejection | Within **90 days** from the expiry of the applicable response timeline or date of last communication from the Regulated Entity, whichever is later |
| **Appellate Authority & Appeal Window** | Executive Director in-charge of CEPD at RBI | **Executive Director in-charge of CEPD at RBI**; appeal must be filed within **30 days of receiving the Award** *(appeal available strictly against an Award, NOT against rejection)* |
| **Regulated Entities Covered** | SCBs, RRBs, StCBs, DCCBs, qualifying NBFCs | SCBs, RRBs, StCBs, DCCBs, UCBs ($\ge ₹50\text{ Cr}$ deposits), NBFCs ($\ge ₹100\text{ Cr}$ assets with customer interface), PPI issuers, Credit Information Companies (CICs) |

---

### 5.4 DICGC Deposit Insurance & 90-Day Resolution Breakdown [RULE-SENSITIVE]

The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) is a **wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI**, governed under the **DICGC Act, 1961** (Authorized capital: ₹50 Crore).
- **Insurance Coverage Limit**: Up to **₹5,00,000 (₹5 Lakh)** per depositor per insured bank in the **same right and same capacity**, covering both **principal and interest combined**.
- **Cross-Branch Aggregation Rule**: Deposits across all branches of the *same insured bank* are aggregated together. Having accounts in 5 different branches of SBI provides a single composite cover of ₹5 Lakh, not 5 × ₹5 Lakh. Different legal capacities (e.g., individual savings vs partner in a firm) qualify for separate ₹5 Lakh limits.
- **Excluded Deposits**: Deposits of foreign governments, central/state governments, interbank deposits, and state land development banks.

#### The Statutory 90-Day Moratorium Resolution Timeline (Section 18A)
```
Day 0: RBI Direction / Moratorium
  │
  ├─► Stage 1 (Days 1–45):   Insured Distressed Bank compiles & submits depositor claim list [45 Days]
  │
  ├─► Stage 2 (Days 46–75):  DICGC audits, processes & verifies claim ledgers               [30 Days]
  │
  └─► Stage 3 (Days 76–90):  DICGC disburses funds directly to depositor bank accounts     [15 Days]
                             ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
                             Total Mandatory Statutory Resolution Limit = Exactly 90 Days
```

> ⚠️ **EXAM ANGLE:**
> - **Ombudsman Compensation Slabs**: Direct financial loss ceiling is **₹30 Lakh**; mental anguish ceiling is **₹3 Lakh** (Composite max: **₹33 Lakh** under RB-IOS 2026).
> - **Ombudsman Appeal Window**: **30 days** against an *Award* only (cannot appeal against a complaint rejection).
> - **Failed ATM Reversal SLA**: **T+5 calendar days**; delay compensation is **₹100 per day**.
> - **DICGC 90-Day Formula**: Bank submits list in **45 days** + DICGC verifies in **30 days** + Disbursement within **15 days** = **90 days total**.

---24:T1bfe,### 6.1 Basel III Capital Adequacy Framework [RULE-SENSITIVE]

Bank capital functions as an equity cushion absorbing credit, market, and operational losses to prevent depositor loss and systemic panic. Basel capital adequacy is evaluated against **Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA)**, not gross balance-sheet assets.

$$\mathbf{Capital\ Adequacy\ Ratio\ (CRAR)\ [CAR] = \frac{Eligible\ Regulatory\ Capital\ (Tier\ 1 + Tier\ 2)}{Risk\text{-}Weighted\ Assets\ (RWA)} \times 100}$$

#### Basel III Global Standards vs. Mandated RBI Floors for Indian Commercial Banks
| Capital Metric / Ratio | Basel III Global Accord Baseline | Mandated RBI Floor for Indian SCBs | Structural Function & Quality |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1)** | **4.50%** | **5.50%** | Highest loss-absorbing going-concern capital (equity shares, retained earnings) |
| **Additional Tier 1 (AT1)** | **1.50%** | **1.50%** | Perpetual non-cumulative debt instruments with loss-absorption write-down features |
| **Total Tier 1 Capital** | **6.00%** | **7.00%** | Composite going-concern capital (CET1 + AT1) |
| **Tier 2 Capital** | **2.00%** | **2.00%** | Gone-concern supplementary capital (subordinated debt, eligible revaluation reserves) |
| **Minimum Base Total Capital** | **8.00%** | **9.00%** | Minimum statutory capital baseline before mandatory buffers |
| **Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB)** | **2.50%** | **2.50%** | Maintained strictly in Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital |
| **Total Capital including CCB** | **10.50%** | **11.50%** | Comprehensive regulatory capital requirement before D-SIB surcharges |
| **Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR)** | $\ge$ **100%** | $\ge$ **100%** | High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) to cover net cash outflows over **30 calendar days** |
| **Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR)** | $\ge$ **100%** | $\ge$ **100%** | Structural resilience over a **1-year horizon**: $\frac{\text{Available Stable Funding}}{\text{Required Stable Funding}} \ge 100\%$ |
| **Leverage Ratio** | **3.00%** | **4.00% for D-SIBs**<br>**3.50% other banks** | Non-risk-weighted backstop: $\frac{\text{Tier 1 Capital}}{\text{Total Exposure Measure}} \times 100$ |

> 💡 **Critical Examiner Trap Resolved:** The Basel Committee's global baseline for total minimum capital is **8.0%** (10.5% with CCB). The **9.0%** figure is an India-specific prudential requirement established by the RBI, which pushes the total Indian commercial bank requirement to **11.5%** with CCB.

---

### 6.2 Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) [RULE-SENSITIVE]

Banks whose failure would cause catastrophic disruption to the domestic financial system are designated as **Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs)**.
- **Assessment Trigger**: Banks whose total balance-sheet size exceeds **2% of national GDP**.
- **Scoring Parameters & Regulatory Weightages**:
  - **Size**: **40%** weightage.
  - **Interconnectedness**: **20%** weightage.
  - **Substitutability / Financial Infrastructure**: **20%** weightage.
  - **Complexity**: **20%** weightage.

#### D-SIB Buckets & Additional Capital Surcharges
| D-SIB Bucket | Additional CET1 Surcharge (% of RWA) | Designated Bank(s) in India | Total Minimum CET1 Requirement (Base 5.5% + CCB 2.5% + Surcharge) |
| :---: | :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **Bucket 5** | **1.00%** | *Currently Empty* | 9.00% |
| **Bucket 4** | **0.80%** | **State Bank of India (SBI)** | **8.80%** |
| **Bucket 3** | **0.60%** | *Currently Empty* | 8.60% |
| **Bucket 2** | **0.40%** | **HDFC Bank** | **8.40%** |
| **Bucket 1** | **0.20%** | **ICICI Bank** | **8.20%** |

### 6.3 Delinquency Ladder, Asset Classification & Provisioning Matrix [RULE-SENSITIVE]

| Classification Category | Delinquency / Overdue Timeline | Provisioning Norm (Secured Exposure) | Provisioning Norm (Unsecured Exposure) | Operational Status & Accounting Treatment |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **Standard Asset** | Serviced regularly; **0 days** overdue | **0.25% to 1.00%** *(General)* | Same | Normal performing asset; interest recognized on accrual basis |
| **SMA-0** *(Special Mention)* | Overdue for **1 to 30 days** | Standard provision | Standard provision | Early stress alert trigger (Principal or Interest) |
| **SMA-1** | Overdue for **31 to 60 days** | Standard provision | Standard provision | Intermediate default warning stage |
| **SMA-2** | Overdue for **61 to 90 days** | Standard provision | Standard provision | Advanced pre-NPA default stage |
| **Non-Performing Asset (NPA)** | Overdue for **more than 90 days** | Ceases to accrue income on accrual basis | Ceases to accrue income | Interest recognized only upon **actual cash realization**.<br>• **Agri Loans**: Overdue for **2 crop seasons** (short-duration crops) or **1 crop season** (long-duration crops) |
| **Substandard Asset** | Remained an NPA for $\le$ **12 months** | **15.00%** | **25.00%** | First NPA category; credit weakness evident |
| **Doubtful Asset — D1** | Substandard for **up to 1 year** | **25.00%** | **100.00%** | Second NPA category; full recovery highly improbable |
| **Doubtful Asset — D2** | Substandard for **1 to 3 years** | **40.00%** | **100.00%** | Significant structural degradation of underlying security |
| **Doubtful Asset — D3** | Substandard for **exceeding 3 years** | **100.00%** | **100.00%** | 100% provision mandated on entire exposure |
| **Loss Asset** | Uncollectible; identified by bank, auditors, or RBI inspection | **100.00%** *(or complete write-off)* | **100.00%** *(or complete write-off)* | Zero salvageable security value remaining |

### 6.4 Stressed Asset Recovery Legal Infrastructure [FOUNDATION]

* **SARFAESI Act, 2002**: Empowers eligible secured creditors to enforce security interests over mortgaged collateral out-of-court (issuing 60-day demand notices under Section 13(2) and taking possession under Section 13(4)) without filing an ordinary civil suit. Does NOT apply to agricultural land or loans below ₹1 Lakh.
* **Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRTs)**: Established under Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993 for claims of ₹20 Lakh and above across banks and financial institutions.
* **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016**: Creditor-in-control corporate resolution process through Committee of Creditors (CoC) via the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). Default threshold: ₹1 Crore.
* **Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs)**: Specialized entities registered under Section 3 of SARFAESI Act to purchase stressed debt from banks against Security Receipts (SRs) and pursue bad debt resolution.

> ⚠️ **EXAM ANGLE:**
> - **LCR vs NSFR Horizons**: LCR covers a **30-calendar-day** stress period; NSFR covers a **1-year structural horizon**.
> - **D-SIB Surcharges**: SBI = **Bucket 4 (+0.80%)**; HDFC Bank = **Bucket 2 (+0.40%)**; ICICI Bank = **Bucket 1 (+0.20%)**.
> - **Agricultural NPA Triggers**: Term loan overdue for **2 crop seasons** (short-duration crops) or **1 crop season** (long-duration crops).
> - **Doubtful Asset Provisioning**: Secured portion escalates: **D1 = 25%**, **D2 = 40%**, **D3 = 100%**. Unsecured portion is always **100%**.

---25:T1b7c,### 7.1 Small Finance Banks (SFBs) vs Payments Banks (PBs) [RULE-SENSITIVE]

Both differentiated bank models originated from the **Committee on Comprehensive Financial Services for Small Businesses and Low Income Households (chaired by Dr. Nachiket Mor, 2014)**, licensed under Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

| Statutory Parameter | Small Finance Banks (SFBs) | Payments Banks (PBs) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Regulatory Committee** | Usha Thorat Committee (Evaluation) | Nachiket Mor Committee |
| **Minimum Paid-Up Capital** | **₹200 Crore** (₹100 Crore for UCBs transitioning) | **₹100 Crore** |
| **Lending & Credit Operations** | **Fully permitted** to advance loans and extend credit | **STRICTLY PROHIBITED** from lending or extending credit |
| **Credit Cards Issuance** | Permitted to issue Credit Cards | **STRICTLY PROHIBITED** from issuing credit cards *(Debit/ATM cards permitted)* |
| **Customer Deposit Ceiling** | **No ceiling** (unlimited demand and time deposits) | Capped at **₹2,00,000 (₹2 Lakh)** per individual customer at end of day |
| **Deposit Types Accepted** | Demand Deposits (CASA) + Time Deposits (FD/RD) | **Demand Deposits ONLY** (Savings & Current; zero FDs/RDs) |
| **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)** | **60% of ANBC** *(effective FY 2025–26 under PSL Directions, 2025)* | **Not Applicable** (as lending is prohibited) |
| **Loan Concentration Rule** | At least **50% of loan portfolio must be $\le$ ₹25 Lakh** | Not Applicable |
| **Mandatory Rural Branch Quota** | At least **25% branches** in unbanked rural centres | At least **25% physical access points** in unbanked rural areas |
| **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** | Mandatory maintenance with RBI under RBI Act Sec 42 | Mandatory maintenance with RBI under RBI Act Sec 42 |
| **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** | Standard operational SLR (18.00% in G-Secs) | Minimum **75% of demand deposits in G-Secs/T-Bills** (up to 1 year); max 25% in bank deposits |
| **Conversion to Universal Bank** | Eligible after **5 years of satisfactory performance**, minimum net worth **₹1,000 Crore**, and listing | Not eligible for universal commercial bank transition |

### 7.2 Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs) 4-Tier Categorisation [RULE-SENSITIVE]

Constituted on the recommendations of the **N.S. Vishwanathan Committee (2022)**, Urban Co-operative Banks are categorized into a 4-tier regulatory structure based on deposit exposure.

| UCB Regulatory Tier | Deposit Exposure Slabs | Minimum Net Worth Mandate | Mandatory Capital Adequacy (CRAR) | Operative PSL Target |
| :---: | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **Tier 1** | Deposits up to **₹100 Crore** | • Single-District Unit UCBs: **₹2 Crore**<br>• All Other UCBs: **₹5 Crore** | **9.00%** CRAR | **60% of ANBC or CEOBSE**, whichever is higher *(eff. 1 April 2025)* |
| **Tier 2** | Deposits **> ₹100 Crore up to ₹1,000 Crore** | Standard statutory net worth | **12.00%** CRAR | Same 60% PSL mandate |
| **Tier 3** | Deposits **> ₹1,000 Crore up to ₹10,000 Crore** | Standard statutory net worth | **12.00%** CRAR | Same 60% PSL mandate |
| **Tier 4** | Deposits **> ₹10,000 Crore** | Standard statutory net worth | **12.00%** CRAR | Same 60% PSL mandate |

### 7.3 Priority Sector Lending (PSL) Comprehensive Matrix [RULE-SENSITIVE]

Governed under the consolidated **RBI Priority Sector Lending Directions, 2025** (updated 2026), evaluated against **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** or Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBSE), whichever is higher.

#### 1. Eight Recognized Priority Sector Categories:
1. Agriculture (Farm Credit, Agri Infrastructure, Ancillary Activities)
2. Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)
3. Export Credit
4. Education Loans
5. Housing Loans
6. Social Infrastructure
7. Renewable Energy
8. Others (SHGs, JLGs, distressed persons, startup financing)

#### 2. Master PSL Lender Targets:
| Lender Category | Overall PSL Target (% of ANBC / CEOBSE) | Key Mandatory Sub-Targets & Allocations |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Domestic Commercial Banks & Foreign Banks ($\ge$ 20 branches)** | **40% of ANBC** | • **Agriculture**: **18%** (Sub-target: **10%** for Small & Marginal Farmers [SMFs])<br>• **Micro Enterprises**: **7.5%**<br>• **Weaker Sections**: **12%** |
| **Foreign Banks (< 20 branches)** | **40% of ANBC** | Up to **32%** may be in Export Credit; at least **8%** must be in other priority sectors |
| **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)** | **75% of ANBC** | Priority anchored on agriculture, small/marginal farmers, and rural artisans |
| **Small Finance Banks (SFBs)** | **60% of ANBC** | Rationalised from 75% to 60% (effective FY 2025–26) to support portfolio diversification |
| **Primary Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs)** | **60% of ANBC or CEOBSE** | Effective **1 April 2025** under PSL Directions 2025 *(superseded older 75% glide path)* |

* **Shortfall Penalty Allocation**: Shortfall in meeting PSL targets is mandatorily allocated to the **Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF)** maintained by **NABARD**, or specialized development funds with SIDBI, NHB, or MUDRA, earning sub-market interest rates.

### 7.4 DAY-NRLM Women SHG Credit Architecture & Subvention [RULE-SENSITIVE]

The **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)** was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) in June 2011 (restructuring SGSY).
- **Self-Help Group (SHG) Size**: **10 to 20 rural women** (5 to 20 in difficult, remote hilly/tribal terrains and PwD groups).
- **Central Nodal Lead Bank**: **Indian Bank** acts as the Central Nodal Bank for pan-India interest subvention administration across commercial banks, RRBs, and co-operatives.
- **Mandatory Collateral-Free Lending Limit**: **Up to ₹20 Lakh** (enhanced from ₹10 Lakh baseline). RBI directives mandate: **zero collateral, zero margin, and no asset hypothecation** for women SHGs up to ₹20 Lakh.
- **Interest Subvention Structure (FY 2025–26 Slabs)**:
  - **Credit up to ₹3 Lakh**: Lending rate capped at **7.00% p.a.**. Government provides **4.50% interest subvention** directly to banks. Women SHGs receive an additional **3.00% Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI)**, bringing the **effective net borrowing cost down to 4.00% per annum**.
  - **Credit > ₹3 Lakh up to ₹5 Lakh**: Subvention bridges interest rate down to **10.00% per annum**.

> ⚠️ **EXAM ANGLE:**
> - **Payments Bank Balance Cap**: Capped at **₹2,00,000 (₹2 Lakh)**; PBs **CANNOT lend** and **CANNOT issue credit cards**.
> - **SFB Ticket Size Rule**: At least **50% of loans must be $\le$ ₹25 Lakh**.
> - **UCB Tier 1 vs Tiers 2–4 CRAR**: Tier 1 UCBs require **9% CRAR**; Tiers 2, 3, and 4 require **12% CRAR**.
> - **PSL Target Alignment**: RRBs = **75%**; SFBs = **60%**; UCBs = **60%**; Commercial Banks = **40%**.
> - **DAY-NRLM Nodal Bank & Effective Rate**: Central Nodal Bank is **Indian Bank**; effective net interest rate with prompt repayment is **4.00%**.

---26:Tf25,### 8.1 Non-Resident Indian (NRI) Accounts Master Comparison [RULE-SENSITIVE]

| Operating Parameter | NRE (Non-Resident External) Account | NRO (Non-Resident Ordinary) Account | FCNR(B) (Foreign Currency Non-Resident Bank) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Denominated Currency** | Indian Rupees (**INR**) | Indian Rupees (**INR**) | Permitted **Foreign Currency** (USD, GBP, EUR, JPY, CAD, AUD) |
| **Permitted Source of Funds** | Foreign inward remittances in convertible foreign currency | Legitimate domestic Indian earnings (rent, dividends, pension) or foreign remittances | Foreign inward remittances in convertible foreign currency |
| **Permitted Account Types** | Savings, Current, Recurring, Fixed/Term Deposits | Savings, Current, Recurring, Fixed/Term Deposits | **Term / Fixed Deposit ONLY** (Tenor: **1 year to 5 years**; zero savings accounts) |
| **Repatriability (Principal & Interest)** | **Freely and fully repatriable** abroad without any regulatory ceiling | **Restricted**: Repatriation capped up to **USD 1 Million per financial year** (subject to tax compliance) | **Freely and fully repatriable** abroad in foreign currency |
| **Indian Tax Liability** | **100% Tax-Free** in India (exempt from income tax and wealth tax) | **Taxable in India** (Interest subject to TDS at 30% + surcharge/cess, or DTAA rates) | **100% Tax-Free** in India (exempt from Indian tax) |
| **Exchange Rate / Currency Risk** | Borne entirely by the **depositor** (converted to INR at market rates) | Borne entirely by the **depositor** (converted to INR at market rates) | Borne entirely by the **bank** (depositor receives guaranteed foreign currency on maturity) |
| **Joint Account Eligibility** | Jointly with eligible NRIs/PIOs (or resident relative on 'Former or Survivor' basis) | Jointly with resident Indian on 'Former or Survivor' basis | Jointly with eligible NRIs/PIOs |

### 8.2 Interbank International Settlement & Correspondent Banking [FOUNDATION]

| Account Classification | Literal Derivation | Operational Banking Definition | Concrete Banking Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nostro Account** | *"Our account with you"* | Domestic bank's account maintained in an overseas bank in that foreign country's domestic currency | State Bank of India maintaining a USD account with JPMorgan Chase in New York |
| **Vostro Account** | *"Your account with us"* | Foreign bank's account maintained in a domestic Indian bank in Indian Rupees (INR) | JPMorgan Chase maintaining an INR account with State Bank of India in Mumbai |
| **Special Rupee Vostro Account (SRVA)** | Dedicated INR trade rail | Dedicated INR accounts authorized by RBI (July 2022) to settle cross-border trade invoices directly in Indian Rupees, bypassing USD/EUR clearing | Foreign commercial bank holding an INR account with UCO Bank to settle bilateral oil/commodity imports |
| **Loro Account** | *"Their account"* | Third-party domestic bank referencing an account held by another domestic bank with a foreign correspondent (*"their account with you"*) | Bank of Baroda referencing SBI's Nostro account with JPMorgan Chase |
| **Mirror Account** | Internal shadow ledger | Internal shadow ledger maintained by domestic bank to mirror real-time debits, credits, and balances of its overseas Nostro account | SBI Mumbai maintaining internal books matching its New York Nostro ledger |

> ⚠️ **EXAM ANGLE:**
> - **NRO Repatriation Ceiling**: Capped strictly at **USD 1 Million per financial year**. NRE is **unlimited / freely repatriable**.
> - **FCNR(B) Tenor & Currency Risk**: FCNR(B) can only be opened as a **Term Deposit for 1 to 5 years** (no savings accounts); currency exchange risk is borne by the **bank**, NOT the depositor.
> - **Nostro vs Vostro**: Nostro = **Our account with you** (in foreign currency); Vostro = **Your account with us** (in INR).

---27:T13d5,### 9.1 The Seven Fundamental Principles of Insurance [FOUNDATION]

| Principle | Legal Doctrine & Operational Meaning | Exam Nuance & Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Utmost Good Faith** *(Uberrimae Fidei)* | Both insurer and insured must fully disclose all material facts accurately prior to contract formation | Non-disclosure or concealment of material facts renders the insurance contract voidable |
| **2. Insurable Interest** | The insured must possess a legitimate pecuniary or legal relationship to the subject matter, suffering financial loss upon its destruction | Must exist at inception in life insurance; must exist at time of loss in marine insurance; at both times in property insurance |
| **3. Principle of Indemnity** | The insurer promises to restore the insured to the exact financial position enjoyed immediately prior to the loss, preventing commercial profit | Applies to general and property insurance; does **NOT apply to Life Insurance** (human life cannot be monetarily indemnified) |
| **4. Subrogation** | After settling an indemnity claim, the insurer acquires all legal rights and remedies of the insured against liable third parties | Operates strictly as a corollary of indemnity; does NOT apply to life or personal accident insurance |
| **5. Contribution** | Where multiple indemnity policies cover the exact same subject matter, insurers share the loss rateably | Prevents double recovery; does NOT apply to life insurance policies |
| **6. Proximate Cause** *(Causa Proxima)* | The dominant, active, and efficient cause that sets in motion a train of events leading to a loss determines coverage | If the proximate cause is an uninsured/excluded peril, the claim is repudiated |
| **7. Mitigation of Loss** | The insured must take all reasonable and prudent steps to minimize loss or damage during an insured catastrophe | Insured cannot deliberately act negligibly simply because the asset is covered by insurance |

---

### 9.2 Insurance Industry Metrics: Penetration vs Density [FOUNDATION]

* **Insurance Penetration**:
  $$\mathbf{Insurance\ Penetration = \frac{Gross\ Insurance\ Premium\ Written}{Gross\ Domestic\ Product\ (GDP)} \times 100}$$
  Measures the economic depth and significance of the insurance sector relative to national output.
* **Insurance Density**:
  $$\mathbf{Insurance\ Density = \frac{Gross\ Insurance\ Premium\ Written}{Total\ National\ Population}}$$
  Measures per-capita insurance premium expenditure (typically reported internationally in USD).

---

### 9.3 IRDAI Institutional Profile & 100% FDI Overhaul [RULE-SENSITIVE]

* **Statutory Genesis**: Established under **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999** on the recommendations of the **Malhotra Committee (1994)**.
* **Headquarters**: **Hyderabad, Telangana** (relocated from New Delhi in 2001).
* **Strategic National Mission**: **"Insurance for All by 2047"** (marking India's centenary of independence).
* **Insurance Laws Overhaul (100% FDI)**:
  - Enacted via the **Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025** (Presidential assent: 20 December 2025; notified commencement: **5 February 2026**).
  - Permits up to **100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** under the automatic route for Indian insurance companies (up from 74%), subject to prescribed regulatory safeguards.
  - Formally allows **Composite Insurance Licensing** enabling a single corporate insurer to underwrite life, general, and health insurance under a unified charter.

---28:T1be7,### 10.1 Capital Markets Infrastructure & Securities Instruments [FOUNDATION]

* **Primary Market vs Secondary Market**:
  - **Primary Market**: Issuers raise fresh capital directly from investors through Initial Public Offerings (IPOs), Further Public Offerings (FPOs), or Private Placements. Proceeds flow directly to the issuing company.
  - **Secondary Market**: Investors trade already-issued securities among themselves on stock exchanges (BSE, NSE). Trading transfers ownership; proceeds flow to selling investors, not the corporate issuer.
* **Core Market Intermediaries**:
  - **Depositories (NSDL, CDSL)**: Hold securities in electronic/dematerialized form; regulated by SEBI under Depositories Act, 1996.
  - **Depository Participants (DPs)**: Financial institutions/brokers acting as retail access conduits between investors and depositories.
  - **Clearing Corporations (NSCCL, ICCL)**: Provide multilateral clearing, novation, settlement guarantee, and counterparty risk management.
* **Money Market Debt Instruments**:
  - **Commercial Paper (CP)**: Short-term unsecured promissory note issued by highly-rated corporate entities, primary dealers, and AIFIs to meet working capital requirements (tenors: 7 days to 1 year; minimum ₹5 Lakh).
  - **Certificate of Deposit (CD)**: Negotiable, dematerialized money-market instrument issued by scheduled commercial banks against term deposits (tenors: 7 days to 1 year; minimum ₹1 Lakh).

---

### 10.2 SEBI Capital Market Reforms & Risk Guardrails [RULE-SENSITIVE]

* **Equity Settlement Cycle Evolution**:
  - India transitioned from $T+2$ to standard **$T+1$ settlement in January 2023**.
  - SEBI introduced an optional **$T+0$ beta rolling settlement** in March 2024 (trading from 9:15 AM to 1:30 PM, settling funds and securities by 4:30 PM same day), expanded in December 2024 towards instant settlement.
* **Mutual Fund Lite (MF Lite)**:
  - Relaxed, light-touch regulatory framework tailored exclusively for **passively managed schemes** (Index Funds and Exchange Traded Funds [ETFs]), reducing compliance overhead, capital requirements, and disclosure friction. Does NOT apply to actively managed mutual funds.
* **Equity Derivatives (F&O) Market Guardrails (Risk Mitigation)**:
  - **Contract Lot Sizing**: Minimum index derivative contract value enhanced from ₹5 Lakh to **₹15 Lakh to ₹20 Lakh** to curb retail over-leverage.
  - **Weekly Expiries Rationalisation**: Capped at **one benchmark index expiry per exchange per week**.
  - **Upfront Option Premium Collection**: Mandatory upfront collection of option buyer premiums.
  - **Intraday Monitoring**: Real-time snapshot monitoring of index position limits to prevent synthetic manipulation.

---

### 10.3 Master Macroeconomic Base-Year Matrix (2026 Operative Series) [RULE-SENSITIVE]

| Macroeconomic Metric / Index | Operative 2026 Series Base Year | Compiling Authority & Release Date | Key Basket & Structural Revisions | Predecessor Series |
| :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| **Gross Domestic Product (GDP) / GVA** | **Base Year 2022–23** | MoSPI / NSO *(27 February 2026)* | Incorporates updated Supply-Use Tables, MCA-21 database, GST electronic filing data | 2011–12 |
| **Consumer Price Index (CPI - Combined)** | **Base Year 2024 = 100** | MoSPI / NSO *(February 2026)* | Anchored in HCES 2022–23 & 2023–24; **Food & Beverages weight cut from 45.86% to 36.75%** (358 items: 308 goods, 50 services) | 2012 = 100 |
| **Index of Industrial Production (IIP)** | **Base Year 2022–23 = 100** | MoSPI *(June 2026)* | Expanded electronics manufacturing, semiconductors, solar PV modules, and green tech | 2011–12 = 100 |
| **Index of Core Industries (ICI)** | **Base Year 2022–23** | Office of Economic Adviser, DPIIT *(July 2026)* | **Nine Core Industries** (Expanded from 8 with the inclusion of **Iron Ore**) | 2011–12 (8 sectors) |
| **Wholesale Price Index (WPI)** | **Base Year 2022–23** | Office of Economic Adviser, DPIIT | Basket expanded from 697 to 957 items using updated Gross Value of Output (GVO) weights | 2011–12 = 100 |

#### CPI vs WPI Structural & Policy Contrast
* **Services Sector Coverage**: **Included in CPI-Combined** (education, health, transport, communication). **EXCLUDED from WPI** (WPI tracks physical goods and bulk wholesale commodities only).
* **Monetary Policy Anchor**: CPI-Combined is the **exclusive statutory target** of the RBI Monetary Policy Committee under Section 45ZA. WPI is NOT targeted by the MPC.

---

### 10.4 Fiscal Indicators & Public Finance Terminology [FOUNDATION]

* **Revenue Deficit**: Revenue Expenditure minus Revenue Receipts. Measures borrowing incurred to finance everyday consumption expenditure that creates no productive capital asset.
* **Fiscal Deficit**: Total Expenditure minus Total Non-Debt Receipts. Represents the **gross borrowing requirement of the government**.
* **Primary Deficit**: Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments. Indicates the government's borrowing requirement excluding legacy debt-servicing burdens.
* **Direct Tax vs Indirect Tax**: Direct taxes (income tax, corporate tax) are levied directly on income/wealth where impact and incidence fall on the same entity. Indirect taxes (GST, customs) are transaction-based and can be shifted across the supply chain to final consumers.

---

### 10.5 Income Tax Law Transition: 1961 vs 2025 Framework [RULE-SENSITIVE]

The **Income-tax Act, 2025** came into force on **1 April 2026**, replacing the legacy Income-tax Act, 1961, slashing statutory sections from 819 down to 536.

| Legacy Form / Certificate | Classical Purpose | Current Status under Income-tax Act, 2025 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Form 16** | Certificate of TDS on salary | Existing salary TDS certificates mapped to equivalent rules under IT Act, 2025 |
| **Form 16A** | Certificate of TDS on non-salary payments (FD interest, dividends) | Retained under modernized form schema for bank interest and contractual TDS |
| **Form 15G** | Self-declaration for nil TDS for individuals **under 60 years** & HUFs | Requires total income to be below basic exemption limit |
| **Form 15H** | Self-declaration for nil TDS for **senior citizens (60 years and above)** | Computed net tax liability must be zero |
| **Form 26AS & AIS** | Consolidated Annual Information Statement of tax credits and SFTs | Comprehensive electronic statement tracking high-value banking and investment flows |
| **Form 60** | Declaration filed in financial transactions by persons **without a PAN** | Maintained for specified financial transactions under updated reporting rules |

> ⚠️ **EXAM ANGLE:**
> - **Active Macro Base Years**: GDP = **2022–23**; CPI = **2024 = 100**; IIP = **2022–23**; Core Industries = **2022–23** (Iron Ore added as 9th).
> - **Services in Price Indices**: CPI **includes** services; WPI **excludes** services.
> - **MF Lite Scope**: Strictly applies to **passively managed schemes** (Index Funds & ETFs), NOT actively managed equity funds.
> - **Form 15G vs 15H**: 15G is for individuals **under 60 years**; 15H is strictly for **senior citizens (60+)**.

---29:T1b3a,### 11.1 The 12 Schedules of the Constitution of India Master Table [FOUNDATION]

| Constitutional Schedule | Canonical Subject Matter | Key Constitutional Nuance & Historical Amendments |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **First Schedule** | States & Union Territories | Official names, territorial boundaries, and sovereign jurisdictions |
| **Second Schedule** | Emoluments, Allowances & Privileges | President, Governors, Speaker/Deputy Speaker, Judges of SC/HCs, and CAG |
| **Third Schedule** | Forms of Oaths & Affirmations | Union Ministers, MPs, Supreme Court/High Court Judges, State Legislators, CAG |
| **Fourth Schedule** | **Allocation of Seats in Rajya Sabha** | Allocation of seats in Council of States across States and UTs *(Statutory strength: 245 = 233 elected + 12 nominated)* |
| **Fifth Schedule** | Scheduled Areas & Scheduled Tribes | Administration and control of Scheduled Areas and STs in states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram |
| **Sixth Schedule** | Tribal Areas in North-Eastern States | Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) in 4 states: **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram (AMTM)** |
| **Seventh Schedule** | Division of Legislative Powers | Three legislative lists: **List I (Union: 100 items)**, **List II (State: 61 items)**, **List III (Concurrent: 52 items)** |
| **Eighth Schedule** | **Official Recognized Languages** | **22 Languages** *(Originally 14; 21st CAA 1967 added Sindhi; 71st CAA 1992 added Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali; 92nd CAA 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali)* |
| **Ninth Schedule** | Validation of Certain Acts & Regulations | Added by 1st CAA 1951; post-24 April 1973 laws are subject to judicial review under Basic Structure doctrine (*I.R. Coelho Case*) |
| **Tenth Schedule** | **Anti-Defection Law** | Disqualification on grounds of defection *(Added via 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985)* |
| **Eleventh Schedule** | Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) | **29 Functional Subjects** of Panchayats *(Added via 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992)* |
| **Twelfth Schedule** | Municipalities (Urban Local Bodies) | **18 Functional Subjects** of Municipalities *(Added via 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992)* |

### 11.2 Core Financial & Economic Articles of the Constitution [FOUNDATION]

| Article | Subject Matter | Key Mechanism & Voting Rules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Article 112** | **Annual Financial Statement (Union Budget)** | Estimated receipts and expenditure of Government of India presented annually before both Houses of Parliament |
| **Article 246A & 279A** | **Goods & Services Tax (GST) & GST Council** | Introduced by **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016**.<br>• **Article 246A**: Simultaneous taxation power to Parliament and State Legislatures.<br>• **Article 279A**: **GST Council** chaired by Union Finance Minister; Centre holds **1/3rd (33.33%)** voting weight, States hold **2/3rd (66.67%)**; decisions require a **3/4th (75%) majority** |
| **Article 266(1)** | **Consolidated Fund of India / States** | All sovereign revenues, loans raised, and loan recoveries flow here; zero expenditure permitted without Parliamentary appropriation |
| **Article 266(2)** | **Public Account of India / States** | All other public moneys received by government (PF, small savings deposits, judicial deposits); executive withdrawal without legislative vote |
| **Article 267** | **Contingency Fund of India** | Imprest at disposal of President for urgent unforeseen spending pending appropriation *(Corpus: **₹30,000 Crore**)* |
| **Article 280** | **Finance Commission** | Quinquennial commission recommending tax devolution and grants-in-aid *(16th FC chaired by **Dr. Arvind Panagariya** for FY27–FY31)* |
| **Article 300A** | **Right to Property (Constitutional Right)** | Deleted from Fundamental Rights (Art 19(1)(f) & Art 31) and reconstituted as a **Legal / Constitutional Right under Article 300A in Part XII** via **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978** |

### 11.3 Strategic Global Maritime Straits & International Chokepoints [FOUNDATION]

| Strait / Chokepoint | Water Bodies Connected | Landmasses Separated | Strategic Importance & Global Trade Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Strait of Hormuz** | **Persian Gulf** $\longleftrightarrow$ **Gulf of Oman** & Arabian Sea | Iran (North) $\longleftrightarrow$ Oman exclave & UAE (South) | Foremost petroleum transit chokepoint handling ~20% of world petroleum liquids |
| **Bab-el-Mandeb** | **Red Sea** $\longleftrightarrow$ **Gulf of Aden** & Indian Ocean | Yemen (Arabian Peninsula) $\longleftrightarrow$ Djibouti & Eritrea (Horn of Africa) | Southern maritime gateway to the Suez Canal; critical Europe-Asia trade artery |
| **Strait of Malacca** | **Andaman Sea** $\longleftrightarrow$ **South China Sea** | Peninsular Malaysia $\longleftrightarrow$ Indonesian island of Sumatra | Primary sea route connecting Indian Ocean energy supplies to East Asian markets |
| **Turkish Straits** | **Black Sea** $\longleftrightarrow$ **Mediterranean Sea** (via Marmara) | European Turkey $\longleftrightarrow$ Asian Turkey (Anatolia) | Governed internationally by **1936 Montreux Convention**; outlet for Black Sea states |
| **Palk Strait** | **Bay of Bengal** $\longleftrightarrow$ **Palk Bay / Gulf of Mannar** | Tamil Nadu (India) $\longleftrightarrow$ Jaffna Peninsula (Sri Lanka) | Strategic shallow-water international passage separating India and Sri Lanka |

### 11.4 Global Governance & Strategic Bilateral Pacts [FOUNDATION]

* **UNSC Permanent 5 (P5)**: **United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia, China** (hold veto power over substantive resolutions; 10 non-permanent members elected for 2-year terms).
* **Paris Climate Agreement (COP21, 2015)**: Under UNFCCC framework; legally binding treaty aiming to hold global average temperature increase to **well below 2°C** above pre-industrial levels and pursue efforts to **limit it to 1.5°C**.
* **Chabahar Port Agreement**: Located in Sistan-Baluchistan, Iran on the Gulf of Oman. India signed a landmark **10-year bilateral contract on 13 May 2024** via India Ports Global Limited (IPGL) to develop and operate the Shahid Beheshti Terminal, securing transit connectivity to Afghanistan and Central Asia bypassing Pakistan.
* **BIMCO (Baltic and International Maritime Council)**: World's largest non-governmental international shipping association, headquartered in **Copenhagen, Denmark** (est. 1905).

> ⚠️ **EXAM ANGLE:**
> - **Fourth Schedule Trap**: Allocates seats in **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States), NOT Lok Sabha.
> - **Right to Property Status**: It is a **Constitutional/Legal Right under Article 300A**, NOT a Fundamental Right (moved via **44th CAA 1978**).
> - **GST Council Voting**: Centre = **1/3rd (33.33%)**; States = **2/3rd (66.67%)**; Decision threshold = **3/4th (75%) majority**.
> - **Strait of Hormuz**: Connects **Persian Gulf with Gulf of Oman** (not Red Sea).

---2a:T19dd,### 12.1 22 Must-Know Conceptual Distinction Pairs [FOUNDATION]

| Concept Pair | Core Distinction in One Sentence |
| :--- | :--- |
| **CRR vs SLR** | CRR is cash maintained with the RBI (yielding 0% interest); SLR is eligible liquid assets (G-Secs, cash, gold) maintained by the bank itself. |
| **RBI Act vs BR Act** | RBI Act 1934 governs central bank powers, currency issue, and monetary policy; BR Act 1949 regulates commercial banking operations, licensing, and supervision. |
| **Liquidity vs Solvency** | Liquidity is meeting current cash-flow obligations as they fall due; Solvency is having sufficient asset value and capital to exceed total liabilities. |
| **Deposits vs Advances** | Deposits are liabilities (the bank owes depositors); Loans and advances are assets (borrowers owe the bank). |
| **NEFT vs RTGS** | NEFT operates in half-hourly deferred net settlement batches; RTGS settles transactions individually in real time with a ₹2 Lakh minimum. |
| **UPI vs Bank Account** | UPI is an interoperable messaging and payment routing protocol; a bank account is the underlying deposit liability repository. |
| **SFB vs Payments Bank** | SFBs advance loans and accept unlimited deposits; Payments Banks can accept demand deposits up to ₹2 Lakh but are prohibited from lending. |
| **DICGC vs RBI Ombudsman** | DICGC provides deposit insurance up to ₹5 Lakh in liquidation/moratorium; the Ombudsman resolves operational service deficiency complaints. |
| **LCR vs NSFR** | LCR measures 30-day short-term acute cash outflow resilience; NSFR enforces 1-year structural stable balance sheet funding. |
| **Gross NPA vs Net NPA** | Gross NPA is total defaulted loans; Net NPA is Gross NPA minus accumulated loan-loss provisions. |
| **Nostro vs Vostro** | Nostro is our account with a foreign bank in foreign currency; Vostro is a foreign bank's account with us in Indian Rupees. |
| **Primary vs Secondary Market** | In primary markets, corporate issuers raise fresh capital; in secondary markets, investors trade existing securities among themselves. |
| **ETF vs Index Mutual Fund** | ETFs trade continuously throughout the trading day on stock exchanges; index mutual funds transact at end-of-day NAV. |
| **Insurance Penetration vs Density** | Penetration is insurance premium as a percentage of GDP; Density is insurance premium per capita (in USD). |
| **Indemnity vs Life Insurance** | General insurance indemnifies actual financial loss; Life insurance pays a contractually agreed sum assured upon death or maturity. |
| **Consolidated Fund vs Public Account** | Consolidated Fund holds sovereign revenues and borrowings requiring Parliamentary appropriation; Public Account holds fiduciary public moneys. |
| **Fundamental Right vs Article 300A** | Property is a legal/constitutional right under Article 300A, no longer an enforceable Fundamental Right in Part III. |
| **CPI vs WPI** | CPI includes consumer services and serves as the MPC's inflation target; WPI tracks wholesale goods only and excludes services. |
| **M0 vs M1** | M0 includes currency in circulation; M1 includes currency with the public (which excludes vault cash held by commercial banks). |
| **Commercial Paper vs CD** | CPs are issued by corporate entities and primary dealers; CDs are issued by scheduled commercial banks. |
| **T+1 vs T+0 Settlement** | T+1 settles trades on the next business day; T+0 settles cash and securities on the same trade date. |
| **Statute Assent vs Commencement** | An Act receives Presidential assent on one date, but provisions take legal effect on the notified commencement date. |
